notes: Reconciled from coders A and B. Sample statements on the Guide page are mostly from other universities (Tennessee State, Ohio, Penn, USC, etc.) and one from The New School (Design and Technology, Jess Irish); coded as the page states them. The integrity policy's sanction scale is general, not AI-specific, and is kept as one unit. Candidate new type: allow AI for research assistance and finding sources (two UNCOVERED units). Course layer deferred; no school or computing policy found.

documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy
documents.stance_why: The policy says "Only authorized use of artificial intelligence tools is permitted" and lists "unauthorized use of artificial intelligence tools" as dishonesty, so AI is banned unless authorized. Faculty decide what is authorized and must give "direction on the use of generative artificial intelligence tools, if permitted", but the document itself sets the restrictive default, so restrict rather than delegates.
documents.summary: The catalog policy defines academic dishonesty to include unauthorized AI use and allows only authorized use. Faculty must give syllabus direction on generative AI, and students who are unsure ask the instructor.

units.why: The sentence says circumstances 'may require different procedures for citing' AI-generated work, so citation practice varies by context; P04 is the nearest type but this is about citation rather than permission, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: different academic circumstances may require different procedures for citing sources
units.frag_start: The New School recognizes that different
units.fit_note: Says citation procedures for AI-generated work vary by circumstance; it does not say who decides whether AI is allowed. | Only acknowledges that AI citation procedures vary by circumstance; it does not require disclosure.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: all/general/informs/P04/neutral. Coder B: all/general/informs/P24/neutral. Same sentence on citing work 'generated by artificial intelligence tools'; A coded P04 (the rule varies by circumstance and is set by the course), B coded P24 (disclosure). The sentence only says citation procedures vary; it does not require disclosure, so P04 is kept with both fit notes.

units.why: Faculty 'are required to inform students' in syllabi and give 'direction on the use of generative artificial intelligence tools', which is a syllabus-statement duty on instructors (P09).
units.anchor: faculty members are required to inform students of the academic integrity policy
units.frag_start: In their syllabi, faculty members are
units.frag_end: if permitted for use within the course.
units.policy: Faculty members are required to give students in their syllabi direction on the use of generative artificial intelligence tools, if permitted for use within the course.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: instructor/course-start/must/P09/neutral. Coder B: instructor/course-start/must/P09/neutral. Both coded the faculty syllabus requirement. B anchored the general integrity-policy clause and left policy null; A's normalized policy states the AI-specific duty ('direction on the use of generative artificial intelligence tools'), which is what the source says, so A's version is kept.

units.why: 'Only authorized use of artificial intelligence tools is permitted' fixes the fallback: AI use needs authorization. It is addressed to students, applies generally, and is a duty (must), so P06 and restrict.
units.anchor: Only authorized use of artificial intelligence tools is permitted.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: student/general/must-not/P06/restrict. Coder B: student/general/must/P06/restrict. A coded must-not, B coded must. The source says 'Only authorized use of artificial intelligence tools is permitted', a positive duty to use AI only when authorized; the prohibition of unauthorized use is the next unit. Modality is must.

units.why: The list of academic dishonesty names 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence tools' for ideas, images, code or text, so unauthorized AI use is classed as misconduct (P36); P19 is narrower because this covers any portion of work.
units.anchor: unauthorized use of artificial intelligence tools to generate ideas, images, art/design, audio, video, code
units.frag_end: code, or text for any portions of work

units.why: Students 'unsure about acceptable use' of generative AI 'should consult the syllabus ... or speak with the instructor', which is the ask-before-using rule (P10); P78 (follow each course's rules) is only implied.
units.anchor: should consult the syllabus for a course or speak with the instructor

units.why: The sanction range from 'not responsible' to 'Dismissal' is the general outcome scale that applies to AI misuse because unauthorized AI use is listed as dishonesty; it states penalties in advance (P37) but is not AI-specific, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: Outcomes range from
units.policy: Academic integrity outcomes range from not responsible to Academic Integrity Warning, Probation, Suspension and Dismissal.
units.fit_note: General academic-integrity sanction scale; it covers AI misuse only because unauthorized AI use is listed as dishonesty. | General integrity sanctions, not AI-specific.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: admin/when-misuse/informs/P37/neutral. Coder B: admin/when-misuse/informs/P37/neutral. B coded each rung of the sanction ladder (warning, probation, suspension, dismissal) and the plagiarism workshop and appeal right as separate units; the passage is a general integrity sanction scale, not AI-specific. One unit (A's) is kept for the scale; B's extra units are dropped as generic.

documents.unit: Guide to Teaching and Learning (Provost's Office / Faculty Center)
documents.title: AI Sample Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The page offers templates and says "Please feel free to adapt suggested language below", with statements running from "explicitly prohibited unless otherwise noted" to "totally unrestricted" use and "encouraged". It sets no single rule and hands the decision to each instructor, so delegates, with the sample statements listed as tiers.
tiers: Generic statement allowing AI with documentation of use
Generic statement prohibiting AI unless the instructor notes otherwise
Course samples in text-based tools: require consult-first, citation or appendix, brainstorming only, expected or required AI use, writing prohibited
Course samples in image-based tools: limited uses with citation, unrestricted use with acknowledgement
documents.summary: A Faculty Center page encourages instructors to try the tools and discuss AI with students, then gives sample syllabus statements from other institutions and one from The New School. The samples range from bans to encouraged or required use, with disclosure and verification themes.

units.why: Faculty 'are encouraged to play around with different tools' before deciding, which is advice that instructors learn AI before setting a policy (P63).
units.anchor: faculty are encouraged to play around with different tools
units.frag_start: Before deciding how you want students

The sentence says 'faculty are encouraged to play around with different tools', which encourages engagement with AI tools, so encourage.

units.why: The page offers sample statements and says 'feel free to adapt suggested language', so wording is left to each instructor (P04); the statements are templates, not a university rule.

A coded 'we recommend these' (should) and B coded the earlier sentence about the same repository link (informs). They point to the same resource, so one unit is kept, on the sentence that recommends it.
